reconcile.note: Clarke reads the language-divided nations of Genesis 10 as proleptic, describing the outcome of Babel's confusion narrated only afterward in chapter 11.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen presses the seam: chapter 10 already has the earth split into peoples and tongues, then chapter 11 opens on one universal language.

quotes.text: That chapter brought us to a point at which the earth was occupied by different peoples and different tongues; and here (xi. 1) we are suddenly carried back to a time when the whole earth was of one language and one speech.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885 Eng. transl.), on Genesis 10 and Genesis 11:1.

sides.verseText: Of these were the isles of the nations divided in their lands, everyone after his language, after their families, in their nations.

sides.snippet: The whole earth was of one language and of one speech.
